t: Lesson 12 — Steps 10, 14 and 15: the labelers and the camera
html:
One stop past the capper stands an Inline Labeler, a pressure-sensitive dispenser in the mould of a Novexx FLS 204: a web of labels on a liner runs from the unwind reel over the dispensing edge to the rewind, and an applicator presses the peeled label onto the bottle. Its handshake is the one every dispenser has (Start, here Apply; Ready; Error; Label low), and the rules are the same as on a real panel: start only when Ready, treat Error as a fault that needs a person, never step the belt mid-cycle. This chapter writes that handshake for the bottle labeler (step 10), then uses it again for a second dispenser that bands the scrap boxes with hazard tape (step 14), and ends with a camera that checks every bottle (step 15).

Step 10: the labeler

In the app

Guided mode’s lesson 12 is this section: it checks that the lesson’s tags are made, that S10_Label exists, is called from MainRoutine and verifies, and then watches the line while you run it and ticks each result as it happens:

  • A bottle leaves the labeler with a label

Add the JSR above JSR(S3_Index) and write:

Tags this lesson needs

TagTypeKindDescription
Label_AppliedBOOLbase tagLatched when the label is pressed on; cleared when the belt steps
Label_ReadyBOOLalias of Local:2:I.Data.1Labeler ready: web loaded, head home, no fault
Label_FaultBOOLbase tagLatched on the labeler Error input (end of roll or a missed label); Enter clears it
Label_ApplyBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.13Labeler Start: the applicator comes in and presses a label on
Label_PadInBOOLalias of Local:2:I.Data.0Labeler applicator at the end of its stroke (label pressed on)
Label_ErrorBOOLalias of Local:2:I.Data.2Labeler fault: end of roll, or the last cycle found no label
Label_LowBOOLalias of Local:2:I.Data.3Labeler roll low
Label_GreenBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.14Labeler green indicator
Label_AmberBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.15Labeler amber indicator

The rungs

How it fits together

Rung 0 asks for a label in the after-the-shift frame, one bit past the capper (Exist 11, Broken 9), only when the dispenser says Ready, and it is a latch, because Ready drops the moment the head leaves home: an OTE here would start the cycle and cancel it in the next scan. Rung 1 drives Apply while the request stands; rung 2 takes the end-of-stroke switch (Label_PadIn) as “pressed on”, remembers it for this bottle and drops the request so the head returns; rung 3 forgets it when the belt steps. Rung 4 latches a fault on the dispenser’s Error (end of roll, or a cycle that found no label); rung 5 lets Enter acknowledge it. Rungs 6–7 are the frame lights. Step 3’s start rung has checked XIO(Label_Req) since you wrote it, so the belt never steps with the applicator in, and step 1’s housekeeping rung drops the request when the line stops.

Run it

Every capped bottle leaves with a label (Side or 3D view: the band on the body; the unwind reel shrinks as the roll goes down). Set the Labeler’s labels on the roll at start to 3 and run: three labels, then the Error input, the amber lamp and Label_Fault latched, and the line keeps running, bottles leaving bare, because a labeler fault is not a reason to stop a filler. Click the labeler in Run mode to load a new roll (Ready comes back), press Enter, and labeling resumes.

Try it

Make the fault stop the line instead (add XIO(Label_Fault) to step 1’s seal-in) and decide which you would want on a real line. Then switch the Labeler’s Hand to LH and Applicator to Tamp pad in Properties and watch the machine rebuild on the other side of the lane; the program does not change.

How the label goes on. The applicator works the way the machine does, so what you see in 3D is what the handshake means. Wrap-around: the roller arm slides in until it touches the bottle, the bottle turns against the roller and the label wraps on as a band that grows with the stroke, finishing just before PadIn; then the arm comes home. Tamp: the label rides down on the pad and is pressed on in one touch. Blow-on: the label flies the gap on a puff of air. Wipe-on: the dispensing edge feeds the label out as the bottle moves and a brush lays it down.

Watch for

A band that stops part-way round is a cycle that was cut short: Apply dropped before PadIn, which on the bottle line means the belt stepped with the applicator in, or the line was stopped mid-cycle. The bottle leaves with half a label, and the labeler’s own Labeled input stays off for it. On a real dispenser that is a label on the floor and a stop to rethread.

Step 14: hazard tape on the scrap boxes

In the app

Guided mode’s lesson 15 is this section: it checks that the lesson’s tags are made, that S14_Hazard exists, is called from MainRoutine and verifies, and then watches the line while you run it and ticks each result as it happens:

  • A box leaves the dispenser with its hazard band (Haz_Labeler has cycled)
  • A taped box takes glass at the grinder with none logged untaped

The scrap boxes come off Box_Feed blank, and a second dispenser on the box conveyor, Haz_Labeler, bands each one with yellow and black hazard tape on its way to the grinder’s chute: a box of broken glass must say so before anyone picks it up. It is the same Inline Labeler part with What it applies set to hazard tape and a wipe-on applicator: the band is wiped on as the box rolls under the head, so the cycle is started from an eye ten pixels ahead of the head, LS13. The handshake is step 10’s, in a routine of its own, S14_Hazard, called from MainRoutine under step 12 and, like every station, above JSR(S3_Index). Its Labeled input means the box under the head carries tape, so no done bit is kept in the program: the box carries its own.

Tags this lesson needs

TagTypeKindDescription

Haz_DoneBOOLalias of Local:3:I.Data.8The box under the applicator already carries its hazard tape
Haz_ReadyBOOLalias of Local:3:I.Data.4Hazard-tape dispenser ready: web loaded, applicator home, no fault
Haz_FaultBOOLbase tagHazard-tape dispenser fault, latched until Enter
Haz_ReqBOOLbase tagHazard tape requested for the box at LS13 (latched while the applicator cycles)
Haz_ApplyBOOLalias of Local:5:O.Data.5Hazard-tape dispenser: start the wipe-on cycle
Haz_PadInBOOLalias of Local:3:I.Data.3Hazard-tape dispenser: applicator at the end of its stroke
Haz_ErrorBOOLalias of Local:3:I.Data.5Hazard-tape dispenser fault: end of roll, or the last cycle found no tape
Haz_LowBOOLalias of Local:3:I.Data.6Hazard-tape roll low
Haz_GreenBOOLalias of Local:5:O.Data.6Hazard-tape dispenser green indicator
Haz_AmberBOOLalias of Local:5:O.Data.7Hazard-tape dispenser amber indicator

The rungs

Rung 0 latches the request from LS13 for a box with no tape, only while the dispenser is Ready: as in step 10, Ready drops the moment the applicator moves, so a plain OTE would cancel its own cycle. Rung 1 drives the applicator while the request stands; rung 2 drops the request at the end-of-stroke switch. Rungs 3–4 are the fault and its acknowledge, rungs 5–6 the frame lamps. A box that takes glass with no band on it is logged at the grinder, and again if it leaves at Box_Out.

Try it

Set Haz_Labeler’s labels on the roll at start to 2 and run. Two boxes leave banded, then the Error input, the amber lamp and Haz_Fault; the third box reaches the chute blank and the log says so. Load a new roll (click the dispenser in Run mode), press Enter. Then move LS13 to x 480 and watch the band miss: the cycle completes before the box is under the head. An on-the-fly applicator is a timing problem; the eye’s place is part of the program.

Step 15: inspect every bottle

In the app

Guided mode’s lesson 16 is this section: it checks that the lesson’s tags are made, that S15_Inspect exists, is called from MainRoutine and verifies, and then watches the line while you run it and ticks each result as it happens:

  • A bottle is inspected (Insp_Count moves)
  • A passed bottle goes on past the scrap gate (a whole bottle stands there with Reject bit 0 clear and Scrap_Gate stays down)
  • A bottle the camera failed is scrapped (Insp_Reject_Count moves and Scrap_Gate turns for Reject bit 0). Inject a fault to see one: Tools → Inject Machine Fault → labeler web break

Steps 1 to 14 trust the stations: a bottle that stood under the capper is capped, one that stood under the labeler is labeled. A real line checks. A camera stands over the belt one stop past the labeler, the In-Sight of Level 7 with its job set to bottle inspection: cap on, label on, filled to the line. It is Cam1 in I/O Configuration, and a screen of its own, Cam_HMI, stands beside the line showing each result with its picture. The step is S15_Inspect, called from MainRoutine after the hazard tape; the guided lesson’s fix button adds the camera module for you.

The register frame does the work. After the shift, Exist bit 12 is the bottle under the camera, and Broken bit 10 says whether it is whole (a broken one is for the scrap gate already). The step triggers the camera once per stop, keeps the result code for that bottle (0 = pass; bit 0 no cap, bit 1 no label, bit 2 short fill), and latches a verdict, Cam_Bad. Step 4 shifts the verdict into the fourth register, Reject, at the next shift: in the dwell frame, bit 0 is the bottle at the scrap gate and bit 7 the bottle at the divert gate, which is why step 8’s scrap rung has XIC(Reject[0].0) beside Broken[0].11 and its divert rung has XIO(Reject[0].7). A rejected bottle goes to the shredder exactly as a broken one does.

Tags this lesson needs

TagTypeKindDescription
Insp_DoneBOOLbase tagThis stop's bottle has been inspected
Insp_CodeDINTbase tagThe camera's result code for this stop's bottle: 0 pass; bit 0 no cap, bit 1 no label, bit 2 short fill
Shift_ONSBOOLbase tagOne-shot storage: clear the verdict after the shift has taken it
IC_ONSBOOLbase tagOne-shot storage for the inspected count
Insp_CountDINTbase tagBottles inspected
RC_ONSBOOLbase tagOne-shot storage for the rejected count
Insp_Reject_CountDINTbase tagBottles the camera rejected
Cam_Off_TTIMERbase tagThe camera has been off line for 2 s with the line running
CAM_ONSBOOLbase tagOne-shot storage for the camera alarm
Alarm_WordDINTbase tagLatched alarms, one bit each: 0 main conveyor overload, 1 divert conveyor overload, 2 end-of-line check failed (a jam, a lost bottle, tracking out of step), 3 LS1 dark too long (dirty lens or feeder empty), 4 labeler fault, 5 reservoir inlet open but level not rising, 6 case lane drive tripped, 7 packer infeed full
Alarm_UnackBOOLbase tagNew alarm, not yet acknowledged (Reset)
Reset_PBBOOLalias of Local:3:I.Data.12Blue Reset button: acknowledge alarms and clear the ones whose cause is gone

The rungs

How it fits together

Rung 0 enables triggering and the results buffer while the line runs. Rung 1 is the trigger: a whole bottle under the camera, the shift just done, not inspected yet this stop, the belt not stepping, the line running and the camera ready; a latch, because Trigger_Ready drops the moment the camera takes the trigger. It also latches Insp_Req, which step 3’s start rung holds the belt on, the same hold the fill, cap and label requests have. Rung 2 drops Trigger at Trigger_Ack and remembers this stop’s bottle is done. Rung 3 takes the result when Results_Valid rises: the code into Insp_Code, the acknowledge up, and the belt released. One bottle a stop means the result always belongs to the bottle under the camera, so there is no FIFO to keep; rung 4 drops the acknowledge once the camera has dropped Results_Valid. Rung 5 is the verdict: any defect bit latches Cam_Bad. Rung 6 clears the verdict and the code after the shift has taken them, so a stop with no bottle under the camera shifts a 0; rung 7 forgets the inspection when the belt steps. Rungs 8–9 count inspections and rejects for the screen. Rungs 10–12 are the camera’s own alarm, bit 8 of the alarm word: off line for two seconds with the line running, a result lost to a full buffer, or a trigger the camera missed. The line runs on, because an uninspected bottle is not a rejected one; the console shows the fault and you stop and look. Reset clears it once the camera is back.

Try it

Run the line and put Insp_Code, Cam_Bad, Reject[0] and Insp_Reject_Count in Quick Watch: the code is 0 for every whole bottle and the register stays empty. Then Tools → Inject Machine Fault → labeler web break. The labeler’s Ready drops, step 10 stops asking for labels, and the bottles leave it bare: under the camera Insp_Code reads 2 (no label), Cam_Bad latches, and a 1 walks down Reject until the scrap gate swings for a whole, capped, filled bottle with no label. Watch Cam_HMI as it goes: the picture, the code, the verdict. Clear Machine Faults, load a roll and press Enter: the next bottles pass again.

Watch for

A camera triggered while the belt is stepping sees a smear and fails good bottles: that is what the XIO(Conv_Index) in rung 1 and the XIO(Insp_Req) hold in step 3 are for. Without the hold, a result that arrives after the shift belongs to a bottle that has moved on, and the verdict lands on the wrong one. Alarm bit 8 with the line running is the other thing to look for: the camera is not inspecting, every bottle passes, and the only tell is the fault on the console.

rungs.head: S10_Label · Rung 0
rungs.comment: LABEL REQUEST: the registers have just shifted (Dwell.DN); Exist bit 11 is a bottle one stop past the capper and Broken bit 9 says it is whole; it has no label yet, and the dispenser reports Ready (web loaded, head home, no fault). Latched, because Ready drops the moment the head moves
rungs.words: When Exist[0].11 (Bottle present, one bit per stop (LogixPro B3:10). During the dwell: filler 6, capper 9, scrap gate 13, divert gate 20; after the shift (Dwell.DN) one bit higher) is on, Broken[0].9 (Broken bottle (LogixPro B3:30). During the dwell: filler 4, capper 7, scrap gate 11, divert gate 18; after the shift one bit higher) is off, Dwell.DN (the done bit of Dwell: Belt stopped: sensors read, feeder drops a bottle) is on, Label_Applied (Latched when the label is pressed on; cleared when the belt steps) is off, Conv_Index (Latched while the belt steps one pitch) is off, Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on, Label_Ready (Labeler ready: web loaded, head home, no fault) is on and Label_Fault (Latched on the labeler Error input (end of roll or a missed label); Enter clears it) is off, the rung latches Label_Req (Latched while the labeler is asked to apply; cleared at PadIn) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Exist[0].11) Examine If Closed asks: true when Exist[0].11 is on.
  2. XIO(Broken[0].9) Examine If Open asks: true when Broken[0].9 is off.
  3. XIC(Dwell.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Dwell.DN is on.
  4. XIO(Label_Applied) Examine If Open asks: true when Label_Applied is off.
  5. XIO(Conv_Index) Examine If Open asks: true when Conv_Index is off.
  6. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  7. XIC(Label_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Label_Ready is on.
  8. XIO(Label_Fault) Examine If Open asks: true when Label_Fault is off.
  9. OTL(Label_Req) Output Latch does: latches Label_Req on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Label_Req stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

rungs.head: S10_Label · Rung 1
rungs.comment: START: the applicator comes in against the bottle while the request stands

pred.q: Label_Req is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Label_Apply is on.

rungs.words: When Label_Req (Latched while the labeler is asked to apply; cleared at PadIn) is on, the rung turns Label_Apply (Labeler Start: the applicator comes in and presses a label on) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Label_Req) Examine If Closed asks: true when Label_Req is on.
  2. OTE(Label_Apply) Output Energize does: turns Label_Apply on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S10_Label · Rung 2
rungs.comment: PRESSED ON: the end-of-stroke switch says the label is on; remember it for this bottle and drop the request so the head returns

pred.q: Label_Req is off and Label_PadIn is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Label_Applied is left as it was and Label_Req is left as it was. It stops at XIC(Label_Req).

rungs.words: When Label_Req (Latched while the labeler is asked to apply; cleared at PadIn) is on and Label_PadIn (Labeler applicator at the end of its stroke (label pressed on)) is on, the rung latches Label_Applied (Latched when the label is pressed on; cleared when the belt steps) on and unlatches Label_Req.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Label_Req) Examine If Closed asks: true when Label_Req is on.
  2. XIC(Label_PadIn) Examine If Closed asks: true when Label_PadIn is on.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTL(Label_Applied) Output Latch does: latches Label_Applied on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Label_Req) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Label_Req. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: Label_Applied stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: S10_Label · Rung 3
rungs.comment: The belt is stepping: the next bottle is a new bottle
rungs.words: When Conv_Index (Latched while the belt steps one pitch) is on, the rung unlatches Label_Applied (Latched when the label is pressed on; cleared when the belt steps).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Conv_Index) Examine If Closed asks: true when Conv_Index is on.
  2. OTU(Label_Applied) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Label_Applied. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Label_Applied when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: S10_Label · Rung 4
rungs.comment: FAULT: end of roll, or a cycle that found no label. Latched: a fault needs a person. Click the labeler in Run mode to load a new roll, then Enter

pred.q: Label_Error is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Label_Fault latches on.

rungs.words: When Label_Error (Labeler fault: end of roll, or the last cycle found no label) is on, the rung latches Label_Fault (Latched on the labeler Error input (end of roll or a missed label); Enter clears it) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Label_Error) Examine If Closed asks: true when Label_Error is on.
  2. OTL(Label_Fault) Output Latch does: latches Label_Fault on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Label_Fault stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: S10_Label · Rung 5
rungs.comment: Enter acknowledges the labeler fault (it also clears the counts, step 9)
rungs.words: When Enter (Thumbwheel Enter button) is on, the rung unlatches Label_Fault (Latched on the labeler Error input (end of roll or a missed label); Enter clears it).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Enter) Examine If Closed asks: true when Enter is on.
  2. OTU(Label_Fault) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Label_Fault. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Label_Fault when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: S10_Label · Rung 6
rungs.comment: GREEN on the dispenser frame: running, ready, labels on the roll

pred.q: Line_Run is on, Label_Ready is on and Label_Low is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Label_Green is off. It stops at XIO(Label_Low).

rungs.words: When Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on, Label_Ready (Labeler ready: web loaded, head home, no fault) is on and Label_Low (Labeler roll low) is off, the rung turns Label_Green (Labeler green indicator) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  2. XIC(Label_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Label_Ready is on.
  3. XIO(Label_Low) Examine If Open asks: true when Label_Low is off.
  4. OTE(Label_Green) Output Energize does: turns Label_Green on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S10_Label · Rung 7
rungs.comment: AMBER: roll low, faulted, or a cycle in progress
rungs.words: When either (Label_Low (Labeler roll low) is on), (Label_Fault (Latched on the labeler Error input (end of roll or a missed label); Enter clears it) is on) or (Label_Req (Latched while the labeler is asked to apply; cleared at PadIn) is on), the rung turns Label_Amber (Labeler amber indicator) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Label_Low) Examine If Closed asks: true when Label_Low is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Label_Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when Label_Fault is on.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Label_Req) Examine If Closed asks: true when Label_Req is on.
  2. OTE(Label_Amber) Output Energize does: turns Label_Amber on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S14_Hazard · Rung 0
rungs.comment: TAPE REQUEST: a box at the dispenser's eye (LS13) with no tape on it yet, the line running and the dispenser Ready (web loaded, applicator home, no fault). Latched, because Ready drops as soon as the applicator moves

pred.q: LS13 is on, Haz_Done is off, Line_Run is on, Haz_Ready is on and Haz_Fault is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Haz_Req latches on.

rungs.words: When LS13 (Box at the hazard-tape dispenser) is on, Haz_Done (The box under the applicator already carries its hazard tape) is off, Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on, Haz_Ready (Hazard-tape dispenser ready: web loaded, applicator home, no fault) is on and Haz_Fault (Hazard-tape dispenser fault, latched until Enter) is off, the rung latches Haz_Req (Hazard tape requested for the box at LS13 (latched while the applicator cycles)) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(LS13) Examine If Closed asks: true when LS13 is on.
  2. XIO(Haz_Done) Examine If Open asks: true when Haz_Done is off.
  3. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  4. XIC(Haz_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Haz_Ready is on.
  5. XIO(Haz_Fault) Examine If Open asks: true when Haz_Fault is off.
  6. OTL(Haz_Req) Output Latch does: latches Haz_Req on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Haz_Req stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: S14_Hazard · Rung 1
rungs.comment: START: the wipe-on applicator comes down to the box while the request stands; the band is wiped on as the box rolls under it
rungs.words: When Haz_Req (Hazard tape requested for the box at LS13 (latched while the applicator cycles)) is on, the rung turns Haz_Apply (Hazard-tape dispenser: start the wipe-on cycle) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Haz_Req) Examine If Closed asks: true when Haz_Req is on.
  2. OTE(Haz_Apply) Output Energize does: turns Haz_Apply on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S14_Hazard · Rung 2
rungs.comment: CYCLE COMPLETE: the end-of-stroke switch; drop the request so the applicator lifts. No done bit is needed here: the box carries its own (Haz_Done is the dispenser seeing tape on the box under it), and the next box is a new box

pred.q: Haz_Req is off and Haz_PadIn is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Haz_Req is left as it was. It stops at XIC(Haz_Req).

rungs.words: When Haz_Req (Hazard tape requested for the box at LS13 (latched while the applicator cycles)) is on and Haz_PadIn (Hazard-tape dispenser: applicator at the end of its stroke) is on, the rung unlatches Haz_Req.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Haz_Req) Examine If Closed asks: true when Haz_Req is on.
  2. XIC(Haz_PadIn) Examine If Closed asks: true when Haz_PadIn is on.
  3. OTU(Haz_Req) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Haz_Req. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Haz_Req when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.comment: FAULT: end of roll, or a cycle that found no tape. Latched: a fault needs a person. Click the dispenser in Run mode to load a new roll, then Enter
rungs.words: When Haz_Error (Hazard-tape dispenser fault: end of roll, or the last cycle found no tape) is on, the rung latches Haz_Fault (Hazard-tape dispenser fault, latched until Enter) on.
rungs.ltr:

  2. OTL(Haz_Fault) Output Latch does: latches Haz_Fault on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

rungs.comment: Enter acknowledges the fault

pred.q: Enter is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Haz_Fault is unlatched.

rungs.words: When Enter (Thumbwheel Enter button) is on, the rung unlatches Haz_Fault (Hazard-tape dispenser fault, latched until Enter).

  2. OTU(Haz_Fault) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Haz_Fault. It only ever clears the bit.

rungs.head: S14_Hazard · Rung 5
rungs.comment: GREEN on the dispenser frame: running, ready, tape on the roll
rungs.words: When Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on, Haz_Ready (Hazard-tape dispenser ready: web loaded, applicator home, no fault) is on and Haz_Low (Hazard-tape roll low) is off, the rung turns Haz_Green (Hazard-tape dispenser green indicator) on (and off whenever the rung is false).

  2. XIC(Haz_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Haz_Ready is on.
  3. XIO(Haz_Low) Examine If Open asks: true when Haz_Low is off.
  4. OTE(Haz_Green) Output Energize does: turns Haz_Green on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S14_Hazard · Rung 6
rungs.comment: AMBER: roll low, faulted, or a cycle in progress

pred.q: Haz_Low is off, Haz_Fault is off and Haz_Req is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Haz_Amber is off. None of the branch’s paths is true.

rungs.words: When either (Haz_Low (Hazard-tape roll low) is on), (Haz_Fault (Hazard-tape dispenser fault, latched until Enter) is on) or (Haz_Req (Hazard tape requested for the box at LS13 (latched while the applicator cycles)) is on), the rung turns Haz_Amber (Hazard-tape dispenser amber indicator) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Haz_Low) Examine If Closed asks: true when Haz_Low is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Haz_Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when Haz_Fault is on.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Haz_Req) Examine If Closed asks: true when Haz_Req is on.
  2. OTE(Haz_Amber) Output Energize does: turns Haz_Amber on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S15_Inspect · Rung 0
rungs.comment: CAMERA SETUP: triggering enabled and results buffered while the line runs. The camera is Cam1 in I/O Configuration, an In-Sight over the belt one stop past the labeler

pred.q: Line_Run is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable is on and Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable is on.

rungs.words: When Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on, the rung turns Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false) and turns Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable) Output Energize does: turns Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable) Output Energize does: turns Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S15_Inspect · Rung 1
rungs.comment: TRIGGER once per stop: after the shift, Exist bit 12 is a bottle under the camera and Broken bit 10 says it is whole; not inspected yet this stop, the belt not stepping, and the camera ready for a trigger. Insp_Req holds the belt (step 4) until the result is in
rungs.words: When Exist[0].12 (Bottle present, one bit per stop (LogixPro B3:10). During the dwell: filler 6, capper 9, scrap gate 13, divert gate 20; after the shift (Dwell.DN) one bit higher) is on, Broken[0].10 (Broken bottle (LogixPro B3:30). During the dwell: filler 4, capper 7, scrap gate 11, divert gate 18; after the shift one bit higher) is off, Dwell.DN (the done bit of Dwell: Belt stopped: sensors read, feeder drops a bottle) is on, Insp_Done (This stop's bottle has been inspected) is off, Conv_Index (Latched while the belt steps one pitch) is off, Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on and Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready is on, the rung latches Cam1:O.Trigger on and latches Insp_Req (An inspection is under way: triggered, no result yet (holds the belt)) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Exist[0].12) Examine If Closed asks: true when Exist[0].12 is on.
  2. XIO(Broken[0].10) Examine If Open asks: true when Broken[0].10 is off.
  3. XIC(Dwell.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Dwell.DN is on.
  4. XIO(Insp_Done) Examine If Open asks: true when Insp_Done is off.
  5. XIO(Conv_Index) Examine If Open asks: true when Conv_Index is off.
  6. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  7. XIC(Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready is on.
  8. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTL(Cam1:O.Trigger) Output Latch does: latches Cam1:O.Trigger on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Insp_Req) Output Latch does: latches Insp_Req on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Cam1:O.Trigger stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: S15_Inspect · Rung 2
rungs.comment: The camera has taken the trigger (Trigger_Ack): drop Trigger, and remember this stop's bottle is inspected

pred.q: Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Cam1:O.Trigger is left as it was and Insp_Done is left as it was. It stops at XIC(Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack).

rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack is on, the rung unlatches Cam1:O.Trigger and latches Insp_Done (This stop's bottle has been inspected) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Cam1:O.Trigger) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam1:O.Trigger. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Insp_Done) Output Latch does: latches Insp_Done on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Insp_Done stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: S15_Inspect · Rung 3
rungs.comment: THE RESULT: keep its code (0 = pass; bit 0 no cap, bit 1 no label, bit 2 short fill), acknowledge it, and let the belt go. One bottle per stop, so no FIFO: the code belongs to the bottle under the camera
rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on and Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off, the rung puts Cam1:I.Inspection_Result_Code into Insp_Code (The camera's result code for this stop's bottle: 0 pass; bit 0 no cap, bit 1 no label, bit 2 short fill), latches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack on and unlatches Insp_Req (An inspection is under way: triggered, no result yet (holds the belt)).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam1:I.Results_Valid) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on.
  2. XIO(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off.
  3. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(Cam1:I.Inspection_Result_Code,Insp_Code) Move does: puts Cam1:I.Inspection_Result_Code into Insp_Code. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Output Latch does: latches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(Insp_Req) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Insp_Req. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: S15_Inspect · Rung 4
rungs.comment: The camera has dropped Results_Valid: drop the ack, ready for the next result

pred.q: Cam1:I.Results_Valid is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is unlatched.

rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Results_Valid is off, the rung unlatches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Cam1:I.Results_Valid) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Valid is off.
  2. OTU(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: S15_Inspect · Rung 5
rungs.comment: THE VERDICT: any defect bit set latches Cam_Bad for this stop's bottle. Step 5 shifts it into Reject at the next stop; the scrap gate (step 9) takes the bottle two stops on
rungs.words: When Insp_Done (This stop's bottle has been inspected) is on and Insp_Code (The camera's result code for this stop's bottle: 0 pass; bit 0 no cap, bit 1 no label, bit 2 short fill) is not 0, the rung latches Cam_Bad (The verdict for the bottle at the camera, shifted into Reject at the next stop) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Insp_Done) Examine If Closed asks: true when Insp_Done is on.
  2. NEQ(Insp_Code,0) Not Equal asks: true when Insp_Code is not 0.
  3. OTL(Cam_Bad) Output Latch does: latches Cam_Bad on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Cam_Bad stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: S15_Inspect · Rung 6
rungs.comment: AFTER THE SHIFT has taken the verdict, clear it and the code, so a stop with no bottle under the camera shifts a 0
rungs.words: When Dwell.DN (the done bit of Dwell: Belt stopped: sensors read, feeder drops a bottle) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung unlatches Cam_Bad (The verdict for the bottle at the camera, shifted into Reject at the next stop) and puts 0 into Insp_Code (The camera's result code for this stop's bottle: 0 pass; bit 0 no cap, bit 1 no label, bit 2 short fill).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Dwell.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Dwell.DN is on.
  2. ONS(Shift_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Shift_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Cam_Bad) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam_Bad. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(0,Insp_Code) Move does: puts 0 into Insp_Code. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: S15_Inspect · Rung 7
rungs.comment: The belt is stepping: the next stop brings a new bottle
rungs.words: When Conv_Index (Latched while the belt steps one pitch) is on, the rung unlatches Insp_Done (This stop's bottle has been inspected).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Conv_Index) Examine If Closed asks: true when Conv_Index is on.
  2. OTU(Insp_Done) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Insp_Done. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Insp_Done when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: S15_Inspect · Rung 8
rungs.comment: Count the inspections
rungs.words: When Insp_Done (This stop's bottle has been inspected) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung makes Insp_Count (Bottles inspected) = Insp_Count + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Insp_Done) Examine If Closed asks: true when Insp_Done is on.
  2. ONS(IC_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in IC_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. ADD(Insp_Count,1,Insp_Count) Add does: makes Insp_Count = Insp_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: S15_Inspect · Rung 9
rungs.comment: Count the rejects. The camera's own screen (Cam_HMI) shows each result with the image
rungs.words: When Cam_Bad (The verdict for the bottle at the camera, shifted into Reject at the next stop) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung makes Insp_Reject_Count (Bottles the camera rejected) = Insp_Reject_Count + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam_Bad) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam_Bad is on.
  2. ONS(RC_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in RC_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. ADD(Insp_Reject_Count,1,Insp_Reject_Count) Add does: makes Insp_Reject_Count = Insp_Reject_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: S15_Inspect · Rung 10
rungs.comment: CAMERA OFF LINE for two seconds with the line running (two seconds, so the moment after power-up, before the module has reported in, does not count)

pred.q: Line_Run is off and Cam1:I.Online is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Cam_Off_T is reset to 0. It stops at XIC(Line_Run).

rungs.words: When Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on and Cam1:I.Online is off, the rung runs the timer Cam_Off_T (The camera has been off line for 2 s with the line running) toward 2000 ms (2 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  2. XIO(Cam1:I.Online) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:I.Online is off.
  3. TON(Cam_Off_T,2000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Cam_Off_T toward 2000 ms (2 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Cam_Off_T counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: S15_Inspect · Rung 11
rungs.comment: CAMERA FAULT: bit 8 of the alarm word (step 11 owns bits 0 to 7; the console and the fault lamp show this one the same way). A result lost to a full buffer, a trigger the camera missed, or the camera off line; the line runs on, uninspected bottles are not rejected, so stop and look
rungs.words: When either (Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun is on), (Cam1:I.Missed_Acq is on) or (Cam_Off_T.DN (the done bit of Cam_Off_T: The camera has been off line for 2 s with the line running) is on) and this is the first scan of it, the rung latches Alarm_Word.8 (Latched alarms, one bit each: 0 main conveyor overload, 1 divert conveyor overload, 2 end-of-line check failed (a jam, a lost bottle, tracking out of step), 3 LS1 dark too long (dirty lens or feeder empty), 4 labeler fault, 5 reservoir inlet open but level not rising, 6 case lane drive tripped, 7 packer infeed full) on and latches Alarm_Unack (New alarm, not yet acknowledged (Reset)) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Cam1:I.Missed_Acq) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Missed_Acq is on.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Cam_Off_T.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam_Off_T.DN is on.
  2. ONS(CAM_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in CAM_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTL(Alarm_Word.8) Output Latch does: latches Alarm_Word.8 on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Alarm_Unack) Output Latch does: latches Alarm_Unack on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Alarm_Word.8 stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: S15_Inspect · Rung 12
rungs.comment: Reset clears the camera alarm once the camera is back on line and the buffer has room

pred.q: Reset_PB is on, Cam_Off_T.DN is off and Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Alarm_Word.8 is unlatched.

rungs.words: When Reset_PB (Blue Reset button: acknowledge alarms and clear the ones whose cause is gone) is on, Cam_Off_T.DN (the done bit of Cam_Off_T: The camera has been off line for 2 s with the line running) is off and Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun is off, the rung unlatches Alarm_Word.8 (Latched alarms, one bit each: 0 main conveyor overload, 1 divert conveyor overload, 2 end-of-line check failed (a jam, a lost bottle, tracking out of step), 3 LS1 dark too long (dirty lens or feeder empty), 4 labeler fault, 5 reservoir inlet open but level not rising, 6 case lane drive tripped, 7 packer infeed full).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Reset_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reset_PB is on.
  2. XIO(Cam_Off_T.DN) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam_Off_T.DN is off.
  3. XIO(Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun is off.
  4. OTU(Alarm_Word.8) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Alarm_Word.8. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Alarm_Word.8 when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

Exist.desc: Bottle present, one bit per stop (LogixPro B3:10). During the dwell: filler 6, capper 9, scrap gate 13, divert gate 20; after the shift (Dwell.DN) one bit higher

Broken.desc: Broken bottle (LogixPro B3:30). During the dwell: filler 4, capper 7, scrap gate 11, divert gate 18; after the shift one bit higher

Dwell.desc: Belt stopped: sensors read, feeder drops a bottle

Label_Applied.desc: Latched when the label is pressed on; cleared when the belt steps

Conv_Index.desc: Latched while the belt steps one pitch

Label_Ready.desc: Labeler ready: web loaded, head home, no fault

Label_Fault.desc: Latched on the labeler Error input (end of roll or a missed label); Enter clears it

Label_Req.desc: Latched while the labeler is asked to apply; cleared at PadIn

Label_Apply.desc: Labeler Start: the applicator comes in and presses a label on

Label_PadIn.desc: Labeler applicator at the end of its stroke (label pressed on)

Label_Error.desc: Labeler fault: end of roll, or the last cycle found no label

Haz_Done.desc: The box under the applicator already carries its hazard tape

Haz_Ready.desc: Hazard-tape dispenser ready: web loaded, applicator home, no fault

Haz_Fault.desc: Hazard-tape dispenser fault, latched until Enter

Haz_Req.desc: Hazard tape requested for the box at LS13 (latched while the applicator cycles)

Haz_Apply.desc: Hazard-tape dispenser: start the wipe-on cycle

Haz_PadIn.desc: Hazard-tape dispenser: applicator at the end of its stroke

Haz_Error.desc: Hazard-tape dispenser fault: end of roll, or the last cycle found no tape

Insp_Done.desc: This stop's bottle has been inspected

Insp_Req.desc: An inspection is under way: triggered, no result yet (holds the belt)

Insp_Code.desc: The camera's result code for this stop's bottle: 0 pass; bit 0 no cap, bit 1 no label, bit 2 short fill

Cam_Bad.desc: The verdict for the bottle at the camera, shifted into Reject at the next stop

Shift_ONS.desc: One-shot storage: clear the verdict after the shift has taken it

IC_ONS.desc: One-shot storage for the inspected count

RC_ONS.desc: One-shot storage for the rejected count

Cam_Off_T.desc: The camera has been off line for 2 s with the line running

CAM_ONS.desc: One-shot storage for the camera alarm

Alarm_Word.desc: Latched alarms, one bit each: 0 main conveyor overload, 1 divert conveyor overload, 2 end-of-line check failed (a jam, a lost bottle, tracking out of step), 3 LS1 dark too long (dirty lens or feeder empty), 4 labeler fault, 5 reservoir inlet open but level not rising, 6 case lane drive tripped, 7 packer infeed full

Reset_PB.desc: Blue Reset button: acknowledge alarms and clear the ones whose cause is gone
